== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-04-the-pilot|Aetheric symbols, also referred to as [[Aetheric sigils]], are magical signs that serve as a fundamental component of spellcasting and interaction with the [[Aether]]. Derived from natural patterns within the [[Aether]], these symbols function similarly to a language where meaning is determined by context. Unlike written text that can be processed by machines, these magical signs require a mage to interpret them. They manifest in various visual forms, appearing as flickering sparks, spinning discs, or glowing circles of light in colors such as silver-gray, blue, white, turquoise, pink, orange, and gold. Aetheric symbols are used to create [[magic circle|magic circles]], seals, and protective barriers that can range in [[scale]] from small handheld charms to massive structures spanning miles. They are utilized for diverse purposes, including [[binding]], sealing, summoning, and enchanting artifacts or [[Aethertech]] devices. While many symbols follow common galactic patterns, certain species like the [[D’Niss]] utilize unique variations that resemble insect tracks. Beyond simple spells, these symbols can be etched into environments, arranged in vast patterns across celestial bodies like asteroids, or used to interact with the Aetheric structures of sentient souls.}}

== The Captain ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-01-the-captain|Aetheric symbols are magical signs that require interpretation by a mage. These markings can shine over metal tables, appear as blue-and-red colors, or form white circles and spell-circles. They can be utilized within a spinning disc to analyze spells, or they may flash in turquoise light when arranged in an intricately complex circle. Furthermore, these symbols can be seen reflected in the [[Aether]] during rituals, form a halo around the [[Magic Tower]], or cause [[Aethril]] swords to glow.}}

== The Engineer ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-02-the-engineer|Etched around the major fabricator, Aetheric symbols serve to evoke both creation and alteration. While these markings are notably absent from the [[vault]] and [[Steel Avalanche]]'s uniform, they can be manually sketched in the air by the narrator. During spellcasting, the symbols may manifest as a golden swarm, and they have even been observed arranged within the asteroids of the system. These markings are also utilized for more practical purposes, such as being built into walls to disturb magic or appearing in circles of diagnostic equipment. Additionally, the symbols can be contained within a shining ball that functions as a [[spell-anchor]].}}

== The Knight ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-03-the-knight|Aetheric symbols manifest visually as spinning white or blue circles upon walls and ceilings. Within the [[Prime Arena]], the structural columns are arranged to form letters resembling these symbols, while similar markings have also been etched into windows. These symbols serve a functional role in spellcasting and are susceptible to the effects of titanic clashes occurring in the [[Aether]]. Additionally, they have been known to flash during operations to ensure a pilot remains preserved within the protective systems of a [[Titan]].}}

<li>{{spoiler|book=lh-03-the-knight|[[Aetheric symbols]] were etched into the window.<ref name="lh-03-the-knight-c30">''The Knight'', chapter 30</ref>}}</li>

== The Pilot ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-04-the-pilot|Aetheric symbols serve various magical functions, such as forming a golden chain around a drive during Mariala Brechess{{!}}Mariala's spells or appearing as silver decorations on the hem of her mantle. These markings possess the power to reveal a person's future or be utilized to [[construct]] intricate maps. While [[Kerathin|Archmage Kerathin]] employs them to activate magic, the symbols are susceptible to being melted away by magical eyes or wearing off over time. In one instance, five of these symbols were burned into the sky behind Fathom to complete a [[binding spell]].}}

<div class="wv-facts mw-collapsible mw-collapsed"><div class="wv-facts-head mw-collapsible-toggle">Sourced facts <span class="wv-facts-count">8</span></div>
